title: How long does it take ... ?
subtitle: It takes an hour. It took me three days.
summary: Ask and answer questions about the time a journey or a job needs, with How long does it take ... ? and It takes ... to ...

lesson.heading: How long does it take from ... to ... ?
lesson.text: A plane flies from New York to Washington in one hour. To ask about the time of a journey we say **How long does it take ... ?** The answer begins with **It takes**.

examples.text: How long **does it take** by plane from New York to Washington? - **It takes** an hour.
How long **does it take** by train from London to Manchester?
**It takes** two hours by train from London to Manchester.
How long **does it take** by car from your house to the station? - **It takes** ten minutes.

lesson.heading: Question and answer
rows: It **will take** a long time to ...
lesson.note: Negative: It **doesn't** take long, It **didn't** take long, It **won't** take long.

lesson.heading: How long does it take to do something?
lesson.text: After **take** we use **to** + verb. This works in the present, the past and the future.

examples.text: How long **does it take to cross** the Atlantic by ship?
*A:* I came by train. *B:* Did you? How long **did it take** to get here?
How long **will it take to get** from here to the hotel?

lesson.heading: It takes a long time / It doesn't take long
lesson.text: We can also make a statement about the time something needs. Use **a long time** for a lot of time and **long** in negatives.

examples.text: **It takes** a long time **to learn** a language.
**It doesn't take** long **to cook** an omelette.
**It won't take** long **to fix** the computer.

lesson.heading: How long does it take you to ... ?
lesson.text: To say who needs the time, put **me**, **you**, **Tom**, **us**, **them** after take. A man started reading a book on Monday and finished it on Wednesday evening, so: *It took me three days to read it.*

examples.text: How long **will it take me to learn** to drive?
**It takes Tom** 20 minutes **to get** to work in the morning.
**It took us** an hour **to do** the shopping.
**Did it take you** a long time **to find** a job?
**It will take me** an hour **to cook** dinner.

lesson.text: The sentence always begins with *it*: *It takes two hours*, not ~~Takes two hours~~ or ~~Is two hours~~.

exercises.prompt: How long ___ it take by car from Milan to Rome?
exercises.explanation: The question is about journeys in general, so we use the present simple: does it take.

exercises.prompt: *A:* How long does it take by plane from New York to Washington? *B:* It ___ an hour.
exercises.explanation: it = he/she/it, so the present simple is takes.

exercises.prompt: Cooking an omelette is quick. Which sentence is correct?
options: It doesn't take long to cook an omelette.
It doesn't take long cooking an omelette.
It doesn't take long for cook an omelette.
exercises.explanation: After take long we use to + verb: to cook.

exercises.prompt: Jane found a job. -> How long did it take ___ to find a job?
exercises.explanation: After take we use me/you/him/her/us/them: it took her.

exercises.prompt: Match each situation with the right sentence.

pairs.left: I started the book on Monday and finished it three days later.
pairs.right: It took me three days to read the book.

pairs.left: We left at 10 o'clock and arrived home at 10.20.
pairs.right: It took us 20 minutes to walk home.

pairs.left: I had my first driving lesson in January and passed my test six months later.
pairs.right: It took me six months to learn to drive.

pairs.left: Mark left home at 7 o'clock and got to London at 10.
pairs.right: It took Mark three hours to drive to London.

pairs.left: Lisa began looking for a job a long time ago. She got one last week.
pairs.right: It took Lisa a long time to find a job.

exercises.prompt: You want to know about the train journey from Paris to Geneva. Make the question.
exercises.answer: How long does it take by train from Paris to Geneva?
exercises.explanation: How long + does it take + how you travel + from ... to ...

exercises.prompt: *A:* I walked to the station. *B:* How long did it take ___ to walk to the station?
exercises.explanation: You are speaking to the person, so I becomes you: did it take you.

exercises.prompt: Which form fits the sentence: takes, took or will take?

items.text: It ___ two hours by train from London to Manchester.
It ___ Tom 20 minutes to get to work every morning.
It ___ me three days to read the book last week.
It ___ us an hour to do the shopping yesterday.
It ___ me an hour to cook dinner tonight.
It ___ a long time to learn to drive - maybe a year.

exercises.statement: How long takes it to get to the airport?
exercises.explanation: How long does it take to get to the airport? The question needs does before it.

exercises.prompt: Tom needs 20 minutes to get to work every morning. It ___ 20 minutes to get to work.
exercises.explanation: Put the person after take: It takes Tom 20 minutes.

exercises.prompt: They repaired the computer. Ask about the time.
exercises.answer: How long did it take them to repair the computer?
exercises.explanation: Past question: did it take + them + to + verb.

exercises.prompt: You left at 10 o'clock and arrived home at 10.20. Write the sentence.
exercises.answer: It took us 20 minutes to walk home.
alternatives: It took us 20 minutes to get home.
exercises.explanation: It + took + us + how long + to + verb.
